data.title: The Trinity and Incarnation
data.sourcePassage: Christians believe in one God who exists as three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This belief is called the Trinity. God the Father is the creator of the universe, all-powerful and all-loving. God the Son is Jesus Christ, who Christians believe was God taking human form — this is called the Incarnation. God the Holy Spirit is God's presence active in the world and in believers today. The Trinity is expressed in Christian worship: in baptism, in the creeds, and in many prayers. The Incarnation is celebrated at Christmas, when Christians remember that God entered human history as a vulnerable baby in Bethlehem. Christians believe this act of love shows that God cares deeply for humanity.

data.title: The Resurrection and Salvation
data.sourcePassage: At the heart of Christian belief is the resurrection — the claim that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion. Christians believe this is not simply a past event but the foundation of their hope. Because Jesus conquered death, they believe death is not the end for those who follow him. This hope is called salvation. Christians believe that through Jesus's death and resurrection, the barrier between humanity and God caused by sin has been broken down. Salvation is described as a gift — it is given by God's grace, not earned through good deeds alone. The apostle Paul wrote that if Jesus was not raised from the dead, then Christian faith would be empty. Easter Sunday is the most important day in the Christian year, celebrated with joy, candles, flowers, and the Eucharist.

data.title: Christian Ethics — Love and Service
data.sourcePassage: Jesus taught that the two greatest commandments are to love God with all your heart, soul, and mind, and to love your neighbour as yourself. In the parable of the Good Samaritan, Jesus showed that a 'neighbour' is anyone who needs help — even a stranger from a different background. Christian ethics is shaped by the example of Jesus, the teachings of the Bible, the guidance of the Church, and the inner voice of conscience. The concept of agape — selfless, unconditional love — is central to how Christians believe they should treat others. Many Christians express this through practical action: running food banks, campaigning for justice, visiting the sick, and volunteering in their communities. The Sermon on the Mount contains the Beatitudes, where Jesus said that the peacemakers, the merciful, and those who hunger for justice are blessed.
